sources.title: Treccani: Benevento, historical overview
sources.note: Modern encyclopedia, historical sections: Lombard principality, 1051 papal allegiance, return of princes 1055 and Landulf VI death 1077.

sources.title: Treccani Enciclopedia Italiana: Benevento in the medieval period
sources.note: Older scholarly synthesis, La città nell’epoca medievale e moderna and La battaglia del 1266: papal rectors, surviving statutes 1202, consuls and battle 26 February 1266. Use historical evidence, not its outdated modern statistics.

sources.title: Rotili and Bertelli Buquicchio: Medieval Benevento
sources.note: Scholarly 1992 article, Urbanistica e architettura: houses, over-street connections, December 1092 will/fireplace, crafts and mills; inscription on first capital north corner of Santa Sofia cloister, John IV 1142 to 1176.

sources.title: Municipality of Benevento: Cloister of Santa Sofia
sources.note: Description, twelfth-century rebuilding and sculpted agricultural months June to December. Do not repeat misleading label implying the twelfth-century work was built under Lombard government.

sources.title: Archdiocese of Benevento: Cathedral history and archaeology
sources.note: Final numbered phases: atrium burial area, medieval expansion removing paradiso in twelfth/thirteenth centuries, modern reconstruction.

sources.title: Province of Benevento museum network: Diocesan museum
sources.note: Collection account: ninth-century Lombard princes’ funerary inscriptions reused in twelfth/thirteenth-century facade, recovered after 1943 damage.

sources.title: Giuseppe Viscione: New sculptures for Benevento cathedral
sources.note: ABside 6, 2024, pp23 to 50; abstract directly read: scattered fragments reunited, chronology of presbytery, facade and bronze door revised to second/third quarters of twelfth century. Present as research interpretation.

sources.title: Hill Museum and Manuscript Library: Monte Cassino Exultet roll
sources.note: Institutional teaching facsimile and transcription, British Library Add30337 f8r, 1075 to 1080. Regional comparison explicitly from Montecassino, not made in Benevento city. Latin language/Beneventan script and opposite orientation of text/images; red neumes.

sources.title: Rotili, Rapuano and Lonardo: Medieval ceramics from Sant’Ilario
sources.note: Author-uploaded primary conference article pp693 to 702, indexed full text. Context pp694 to 695: former probable ossuary reused as dump, thirteenth to fifteenth-century assemblage; kitchen/table/storage forms. Later than principality, extends beyond map.

sources.title: Grifa and colleagues: Technological features of Benevento Protomajolica
sources.note: Primary research 2006 pp123 to 133, indexed full repository abstract. Two medieval sites, microscopy/XRF/XRD, likely local production and possible overfired kiln rejects. Do not repeat broad assertion that all Italian glazed ceramics began in thirteenth century.

sources.title: Historical Dictionary of Switzerland: Geneva canton
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis. Introduction, Republic and Society sections: eighteenth-century republic distinct from later canton, inhabitants/natifs without political rights, French annexation April 1798. Territory enlarged1815 to 1816.

sources.title: City of Geneva: Historical route for the Museum of Art and History
sources.note: Institutional museum report, June 2018, printed pp18 to 19: eighteenth-century Fabrique small workshops/export network, indiennes large manufactories, urban development.

sources.title: Wildi and colleagues: Geology and archaeology of Geneva
sources.note: University of Geneva guide 2017, printed p60/PDF index60: Abeille pump 1708 originally seven public fountains. Other histories use1709 or1710; public passage says early 1700s, avoiding spurious exact consistency.

sources.title: Rieder, Suciu and Wenger: Medicine in the street
sources.note: Didactica Historica11/2025, printed p42: private inoculations1749/1750, hospital dependent children February1751, moral objections and risks. No modern treatment instructions.

sources.title: University of Geneva: When medicine entered the academy
sources.note: Historical interview with Philip Rieder, Le siècle qui va tout changer: Tronchin 1754 theory/anatomy demonstrations in short-lived honorary chair, modern faculty much later.

sources.title: UNIL-EPFL scientific instrument collection: Hair hygrometer 603.1018
sources.note: Direct catalogue, date1783 to 1800, maker [Jaques] Paul, inscription Paul à Genève. Parenthetical third-quarter label conflicts with explicit year range; use late eighteenth century.

sources.title: Paul Schule: A dynasty of mechanics and inventors, the Paul family
sources.note: Genava29(1981), pp139 to 149. Indexed full original via query hygromètre cheveu Paul Genève; direct endpoint verification challenge. Hair expands/contracts and moves pointer; Paul built Saussure design. Exact explanatory paragraph begins Il s’agit de fixer un cheveu.

sources.title: University of Geneva: Rousseau’s books condemned
sources.note: 2012 historical commemoration: 19 June 1762 Geneva ordered Emile and Du Contrat social torn and burned before city hall.

sources.title: Geneva judiciary: Eighteenth-century exhibition sheet
sources.note: Official historical exhibition PDF,1794 constitution/jury and limitation of citizenship to Protestant men. Do not translate equality decree as universal adult suffrage.

sources.title: Geneva Grand Council: 500 years of the parliament
sources.note: Official 2026 chronology: French troopsApril 1798 and councils abolished; republic restored 31 December 1813, Swiss canton 1815.

proposedOverrides.summary: Eighteenth-century Geneva was a small republic of workshops, scientific instruments and political arguments, annexed by France in 1798.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Imported 1000 to 1279 record spans principality and papal city. Decoded 1100/1200 footprint reaches Sicily and is grossly false for Benevento; public overview says so plainly. No actual boundary repair asserted. Narrative separates final Lombard phase, papal continuation and later pottery up to fifteenth century. Does not share with earlier composite Lombard cards. Writing is locally attested twelfth-century cloister inscription; Montecassino book is separately named regional comparison.

Imported 1700 to 1800 polygon around Geneva, not all later canton. Public map-window/1798 ending and later-canton boundary distinction. No modern-state substitution. Instrument explicit1783 to 1800 catalogue range has erroneous parenthetical third-quarter-century descriptor; public text conservatively late eighteenth century. Abeille works dated1708/1709/1710 across witnesses; public text early 1700s. No browser used.
